If selected for this position, you will serve as the assistant to the United States Attorney (USA) for the District of Arizona, providing a variety of technical and administrative support services. A confidential relationship is required between the incumbent and the USA.

Typical work assignments will include: Managing and overseeing the day-to-day activities of the immediate office of the USA. Exercising exclusive control over the USA's calendar for all appointments, meetings, engagements, and conferences with complete authority for commitment of time.

Independently handling matters addressed to the USA that do not require personal attention by referring such to appropriate staff members, or personally performing the work needed to resolve the matter. Representing the USA when addressing leading figures with the government, business, law enforcement community, and other organizations.

Arranging conferences and meetings for the USA, preparing agendas and notifying participants. Developing a variety of recurring reports and documents which involve obtaining information from the staff, subject files or other sources, and formatting the needed information properly in narrative, table, or graph formats.

Producing a variety of written documents utilizing varied and advanced functions in one or more types of office automation software. Editing written material for adherence with supervisor's established policies, writing style, and previously expressed views, as well as for conformity with office policies and correspondence procedures.

Responsibilities will increase and assignments will become more complex as your training and experience progress.
GS-10: To be eligible at the GS-10 level, you must have at least ONE year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 level.

Specialized experience is defined as performing complex and confidential administrative support and tasks for superiors; maintaining and exercising control over supervisors' calendar for appointments, meetings, engagements and conferences; reading, screening and controlling incoming documents; receiving and screening visitors and callers; composing a variety of written material; ensuring accuracy of outgoing correspondence for procedural and grammatical accuracy; and making travel arrangements.

At the full performance level, major duties include: Partners effectively with the Executive Assistant to the Chairman to ensure the proper, smooth, and efficient operation of the Office of General Counsel. Oversees the daily operation and function of the Office of the General Counsel.

Prepares letters, correspondence, memoranda, or reports that may include matters of a confidential or sensitive nature.

Serves as liaison with officials of other federal agencies, private organizations, banking officials, members of the public, officers of organizations and others inquiring primarily about the Legal Division's legal and operational matters.

Serves as the General Counsel and Deputy General Counsels' primary gatekeeper and scheduler for internal and external appointments, meetings, conferences, presentations, and speeches.

Makes domestic and international travel arrangements for the General Counsel using the latest office travel planning software and Internet travel tools; and coordinates as necessary with the Division of Finance travel staff.

Serves as timekeeper and performs time and attendance input, generates required reports, and performs leave audits as necessary.
Qualifying experience may be obtained in the private or public sector. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic, religious spiritual; community; student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Additional qualifications information can be found here. To qualify for this position, applicants must have: Specialized Experience: To qualify, applicants must have completed at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the 09 grade level or above in the Federal service.

Specialized experience managing and coordinating an executive level office to include serving as a liaison with internal and external officials, managing meeting calendars and making related travel arrangements; reviewing and analyzing incoming and outgoing correspondence; and serving as a timekeeper for an office or unit.

OR Education: A Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M, if related. OR A qualifying combination of Specialized Experience and Education. For qualification determinations, your resume must contain the following for each work experience listed:
· Organization/Agency's Name
· Title
· Salary (series and grade, if applicable)
· Start and end dates (including the month and year)
· Number of hours you worked per week
· Relevant experience that supports your response to the specialized experience that is stated in the job announcement If your resume does not contain this information, your application may be marked as incomplete, and you may not receive consideration for this position. NOTE: Please indicate how you meet the specialized experience under each applicable position. Do not copy and paste the duties or specialized experience from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications. Applicants must have met the qualification requirements (including selective placement factors – if any) for this position within 30 calendar days of the closing date of this announcement.

· Outspoken and direct — you proactively flag capacity issues and push back professionally when needed
· Flexible and adaptable — comfortable with shifting priorities and ad hoc tasks

· Experience with Recruit CRM Bookkeeping or accounts reconciliation experience

What Success Looks Like

The following are the duties of this position at the full working level. If this vacancy includes more than one grade and you are selected at a lower grade level, you will have the opportunity to learn to perform these duties and receive training to help you grow in this position.

Leads the development, integration, and execution of strategic and operational plans aligned with agency mission and Departmental priorities. Translates executive vision into measurable goals, performance frameworks, and implementation roadmaps.

Establishes governance structures and decision-support processes to ensure alignment across multiple organizational components. Identifies enterprise risks, implementation implications, and resource gaps; formulates mitigation strategies and executive recommendations.

Provides executive-level oversight of priority initiatives and enterprise programs. Monitors performance metrics, deliverables, and compliance requirements. Directs cross-functional coordination to resolve barriers affecting execution. Develops executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to inform leadership decision-making.

Ensures alignment with federal regulations, internal controls, and performance management frameworks. Serves as a principal executive staff resource to assigned HCO leadership in the planning, coordination, and integration of high-priority human capital initiatives and management matters having significant organizational impact.

Provides continuity and coordination across HCO functions and ensures matters requiring executive attention are appropriately analyzed, developed, and positioned for timely leadership action.

Reviews and assesses complex and sensitive matters involving HCO programs, operations, workforce issues, employee relations, organizational priorities, and management initiatives. Identifies interdependencies, conflicting requirements, implementation concerns, and matters requiring resolution or elevation.

Develops assessments, options, recommendations, and executive-level briefing materials to support management deliberations and decisions. Coordinates HCO responses and actions involving IRS organizations and, as appropriate, Treasury, OPM, oversight organizations, and other governmental entities.

Synthesizes information and recommendations from multiple HCO functions and organizational components; identifies unresolved issues or differing positions; and facilitates resolution or presents matters to leadership for decision.

Manages and coordinates executive-level actions arising from inquiries, reviews, audits, organizational initiatives, and other matters requiring HCO leadership attention. Evaluates submissions for completeness, responsiveness, consistency with established requirements and leadership direction, and potential impact on HCO programs and operations.

STANDARD POSITION DESCRIPTIONS (SPD): PD26068 Visit the IRS SPD Library to access the position descriptions.
Federal experience is not required. Experience may have been gained in the public sector, private sector or through Volunteer Service. One year of experience refers to full-time work; part-timework is considered on a prorated basis.

To ensure full credit for your work experience, please indicate dates of employment by month/day/year, and indicate number of hours worked per week, on your resume. You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS: To qualify for this position, you must meet the qualification requirements outlined below: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE GS-15: To be minimally qualified for this position you must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-14) in the Federal Government.

Specialized experience is experience that is related to the work of this position and has provided you with the competencies required for successful job performance.

Specialized experience for this position includes: Experience serving as a trusted advisor to the executive on administrative, operational, and cross-organizational coordination matters impacting Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and departmental priorities, being the central coordination point between the executive office, external partners and interagency partners on sensitive and high-priority matters, and representing the Chief executive, as appropriate, and represent executive in internal coordination meetings and senior-level discussions focused on execution, alignment, and operational follow-through.

Experience with management principles, theories, and practices and their applicability to IRS' programs, functions, objectives, and the development of long-term strategic plans incorporating short-term and long-term goals.

Identify operational gaps, process inefficiencies, and coordination challenges; recommend and implement solutions to improve organizational effectiveness, responsiveness, and execution discipline.

Experience communicating both orally and in writing with internal and external stakeholders to persuade implementation of substantial changes in agency resources and established procedures. Synthesize input from senior leadership, interagency partners, and external stakeholders into clear, concise, and actionable recommendations.

Preparing agency directives, service-wide policy statements, briefing documents, status reports, and other written guidelines and recommendations.

Experience overseeing, coordinating and conducting the development of briefing material, presentations and negotiations on technical problems, outcomes, and recommendations to gain cooperation from top IRS officials and other top officials at federal, state, local, and non-government organizations to improve services provided, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and alignment with strategic objectives.

Establish and maintain effective relationships to gain confidence and cooperation of supervisors, managers, and co-workers to accept proposals.

AND You must also meet the following requirement(s): TIME AFTER COMPETITIVE APPOINTMENT (TACA): By the closing date (or if this is an open continuous announcement, by the cut-off date) specified in this job announcement, current civilian employees must have completed at least 90 days of federal civilian service since their latest non-temporary appointment from a competitive referral certificate, known as time after competitive appointment.

For this requirement, a competitive appointment is one where you applied to and were appointed from an announcement open to "All US Citizens" TIME IN GRADE (TIG): For positions above the GS-05, applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible.

One year (52 weeks) at the next lower grade level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the grade you are applying for. For positions at the GS-05, you cannot advance to the GS-05 if you have held a GS-02 in the past 52 weeks. There is no TIG restriction for GS-02, 03 or 04 positions.

For more information on qualifications please refer to OPM's Qualifications Standards.

Help Us Change the Way the World Works

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations.

Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe's largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows - helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

We’re looking for an experienced, full-time Executive Assistant to join our team in Berlin and support our Co-CEOs, Lennard and Judith.
In this role, you’ll work closely with our Co-CEOs, Lennard and Judith, as part of a young, entrepreneurial team. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, love bringing order to hectic schedules, and approach each day with a proactive mindset, we’d love to meet you.
We’re looking for someone highly organized, calm, self-motivated, and adaptable.

Internal organisation and steering. You run the CEO's operating rhythm. Calendar, inbox triage, meeting preparation, and follow-through all sit with you. You keep an eye on details and you keep the leadership cadence (weeklies, board preparation, offsites) moving.
External travel and speaking. You plan and book complex international travel end to end, and you manage the speaking pipeline: inbound requests, selection, briefing packs, and logistics on the ground.
C-level relationship management. You become the trusted point of contact for the CEO's most important external relationships: customers, partners, and investors. You track who needs a touchpoint and when, and protect these relationships through reliability and proactivity.
Augmentation and anticipation. You work half a step ahead of everyone else in the room. You can identify a bottleneck before it forms. You build the systems, defaults and briefings that let the CEO spend their time on judgement rather than logistics.
Admin. You manage expenses and finance admin and can support with occasional personal assistant (PA) duties as needed.
CEO office collaboration. You’ll work in very close coordination with the CEO office, which includes a Chief of Staff and CEO Office Manager who are responsible for operational processes in the CEO office. Incl. performance management, KPI tracking, leadership accountability and strategic projects.
You Might Be a Fit If…
You have previously supported a CEO or equivalent in a demanding organisation and are looking for another environment that gives you an opportunity to grow.
You want to be in a young, fast company. You are comfortable with ambiguity, short timelines and a team that is still writing its own playbook, and you would rather shape the system than inherit a finished one.
You are mission-driven. You care that European companies build and adopt AI, and you want your work to count toward that rather than toward a job title. You are eager to automate your own work where possible.
AI can do a lot of things, but in the short term, it won't be able to shepherd a growing group of mostly young people in a very dynamic environment. We are looking for someone who can foster the most important human qualities within the organization.
We are looking for a long-term partner, not someone optimizing for their next role.
Personified calmness – You bring order, not chaos. When things get hectic, you're the person who slows down, thinks clearly, and helps others do the same. Your presence makes people feel like things are under control. You instill calmness and continuity in the organization.
Good judgment – You know what matters and what doesn't. You read people well. You understand when to push and when to give space, when something is urgent and when it can wait.
Compassionate and empathetic – You care about the people around you. You understand that behind every missed deadline or dropped ball is a human with hidden context. You hold people accountable with kindness.
Ownership mentality – You see problems and fix them without being asked. You don't wait for permission. You follow through.
Strong communicator – Written and verbal. You can draft important emails or have a difficult conversation with equal skill.
Trustworthy – You'll have access to everything and work directly with the CEO. Discretion and trust are very important.
You are a kind person who cares about the people around you.
The Environment
We work from our office in Berlin, Greifswalder Strasse 212. Everyone works together in person because the hardest problems get solved faster at a whiteboard than in a Slack thread. Conversations happen faster, problems get solved quicker, and we actually know each other.
Days start at 8:30. Lunch & dinner are together. We run, go to the gym, and take care of ourselves. Health is not separate from work here, it is part of how we work well.
The vibe is calm but intense. No one is yelling or panicking. But everyone is working hard on things that matter.

Le Conseil œcuménique des Églises (COE) recherche un Coordinateur Général dynamique et expérimenté pour diriger la coordination sur le terrain de son programme en Syrie portant sur la médiation civique, la cohésion sociale et la construction d'une paix inclusive.

Travaillant en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe basée à Genève, GOPA-DERD\[1\], et MARS\[2\], le Coordinateur Général jouera un rôle central dans le soutien d'un mécanisme national de dialogue et de coordination reliant les leaders religieux, les acteurs civiques et les initiatives locales de construction de la paix à travers la Syrie.
Le poste combine coordination stratégique, développement de relations, gestion de projet et accompagnement des initiatives de paix menées localement, avec un accent particulier sur le dialogue, la médiation, l'identification précoce des tensions communautaires et le soutien à une participation civique inclusive durant la transition syrienne.

**Responsabilités principales**
* Coordonner la mise en œuvre globale du programme Syrie du COE en étroite coopération avec le bureau de Genève, en assurant la cohérence entre les objectifs stratégiques, les plans de travail et la mise en œuvre sur le terrain.
* Coordonner et faciliter un mécanisme national de dialogue et de coordination qui favorise la confiance et l'action collaborative entre acteurs religieux et civiques, garantissant une participation inclusive et constructive.
* Renforcer la collaboration entre le mécanisme national de coordination et les structures locales de coordination, en veillant à ce que les expériences locales, l'analyse des conflits et les efforts de médiation alimentent le dialogue national et vice versa.
* Superviser et accompagner les coordinateurs nationaux, régionaux et locaux, en fournissant des conseils techniques, du mentorat et un suivi régulier.
* Coordonner étroitement avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre, y compris GOPA-DERD et MARS, ainsi qu'avec les consultants et experts engagés dans la mise en œuvre du programme.
* Maintenir une communication régulière avec l'équipe de Genève, en fournissant des mises à jour stratégiques, en identifiant les risques et opportunités émergents, et en soutenant la gestion adaptative du programme.
* Faciliter l'engagement avec les leaders religieux, les organisations de la société civile, les représentants communautaires, les autorités locales et autres parties prenantes pertinentes, conformément aux principes de neutralité, d'inclusivité et de dialogue du COE.
* Soutenir des initiatives discrètes de médiation et de renforcement de la confiance, y compris l'accompagnement de questions communautaires sensibles lorsque cela est approprié.
* Superviser la planification, le suivi, le reporting et la documentation du programme, en assurant des contributions de qualité et en temps utile aux rapports des bailleurs et aux processus d'apprentissage.

* Veiller à ce que les approches sensibles aux conflits, de protection, de « Ne pas nuire » et inclusives soient intégrées dans toutes les activités et partenariats du programme.

* Capacité et volonté de voyager en Syrie.

## À propos du Département des Affaires étrangères et du Commerce ##
Le rôle du Département des Affaires étrangères et du Commerce (DFAT) est de promouvoir les intérêts de l'Australie et des Australiens à l'international.

Cela implique de renforcer la sécurité de l'Australie, d'améliorer sa prospérité, de fournir un programme d'aide étrangère efficace et de haute qualité, et d'aider les voyageurs australiens ainsi que les Australiens à l'étranger. Le département fournit des conseils en politique étrangère, commerciale et de développement au gouvernement australien.

Le DFAT collabore également avec d'autres agences gouvernementales australiennes pour coordonner la poursuite des intérêts globaux, régionaux et bilatéraux de l'Australie.
## À propos du poste ##
Sous la direction, l'Assistant Exécutif de l'Ambassadeur et du Vice-Ambassadeur fournit un soutien exécutif, administratif et organisationnel de haut niveau à la Mission Permanente d'Australie auprès des Nations Unies à Genève. Le poste organise également des événements et fonctions officiels.
En raison de la nature sensible du travail, ce poste nécessite de pouvoir obtenir et maintenir une habilitation de sécurité nationale reconnue par le DFAT.
## Les principales responsabilités du poste incluent, sans s'y limiter : ##
* Fournir un soutien exécutif de haut niveau à l'Ambassadeur et au Vice-Ambassadeur, assurant le bon fonctionnement des bureaux exécutifs dans un environnement rapide et sensible.
* Gérer et prioriser la correspondance, les invitations, les documents d'information et les demandes, en faisant preuve d'un jugement avisé pour déterminer les priorités, les actions et les exigences de conformité.
* Coordonner les visites officielles et les programmes de délégation pour les ministres, hauts fonctionnaires et visiteurs de haut niveau, en équilibrant les priorités concurrentes et les exigences opérationnelles.
* Planifier et organiser des événements de représentation, des réunions et des engagements officiels, en liaison avec les parties prenantes internes et externes pour atteindre les objectifs de la Mission.
* Gérer les dépenses de représentation et l'administration financière, y compris les prévisions, les justifications, les rapprochements et les rapports conformément aux politiques et procédures du DFAT.
* Coordonner les déplacements, la logistique et les arrangements administratifs liés aux activités de la direction exécutive et officielles, en assurant la conformité aux politiques et procédures pertinentes.
* Surveiller les risques liés à la sécurité, aux opérations et au flux de travail, en mettant en œuvre les contrôles nécessaires et en escaladant les problèmes le cas échéant.
* Fournir des conseils administratifs, maintenir des systèmes d'affaires efficaces et soutenir la coordination de l'équipe, contribuant à l'amélioration continue et à l'efficacité organisationnelle.
## Qualifications/Expérience/Connaissances/Compétences requises ##
* Expérience avérée dans un rôle similaire d'Assistant Exécutif
* Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale
* Capacité à travailler en équipe et à soutenir celle-ci. Capacité à développer et maintenir des relations respectueuses et efficaces avec les parties prenantes internes et externes
* Capacité à gérer le temps, à prioriser, planifier, gérer plusieurs tâches et travailler efficacement sous pression
* Compétences en gestion financière et organisationnelle
* Discrétion et jugement avisé dans la gestion d'informations confidentielles
* Expérience étendue de l'utilisation de Microsoft Office et des applications électroniques
* Compétences exceptionnelles en service client et en relations interpersonnelles
* Maîtrise de l'anglais requise, la maîtrise du français étant fortement appréciée
* Connaissance ou capacité à acquérir rapidement une connaissance de la législation du gouvernement australien ou des politiques et directives départementales relatives aux fonctions du poste
## Souhaitable ##
* Expérience préalable dans une ambassade, une organisation internationale ou un environnement comparable.
## Exigences de sécurité ##
* Habilitation de sécurité NV2 australienne ou capacité à l'obtenir et la maintenir. Les candidats doivent donc être citoyens australiens pour être considérés.
* Veuillez noter que les candidats détenant la citoyenneté ou la double citoyenneté suisse ne sont pas éligibles à une habilitation de sécurité australienne.

Ihre neue Rolle
Als Sekretär/in der Geschäftsprüfungskommission (GPK) sind Sie Teil des Teams der Finanzkontrolle, welche neben Ihrer Revisionstätigkeit auch das Sekretariat der Geschäftsprüfungskommission des Stadtparlaments führt. In Ihrer Rolle sind Sie für die Organisation der monatlichen GPK\-Sitzungen verantwortlich.

Als Vorbereitung stellen Sie eigenständig einen Traktandenvorschlag zusammen und bereiten sämtliche Unterlagen auf. Während den Sitzungen stellen Sie die anspruchsvolle und umfassende Protokollführung sicher.

Zudem beraten und unterstützen Sie den Präsidenten / die Präsidentin und die Mitglieder der Geschäftsprüfungskommission bei verschiedenen Anliegen. Sie unterstützen die GPK bei der Erarbeitung von Anträgen und stellen den Informationsfluss zwischen der Kommission, dem Stadtrat und der Verwaltung sicher.

Für diese interessante Funktion sind Kenntnisse über Organisation, Abläufe und Rechnungswesen in einer öffentlichen Verwaltung von Vorteil, jedoch keine Voraussetzung.
Diese Stelle ist für Sie, wenn
Sie über eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung im kaufmännischen Bereich verfügen und bereits einige Jahre Berufserfahrung in einer vergleichbaren Position (z.B. Direktionsassistenz) mitbringen.
Ihnen das Organisieren von Sitzungen, anspruchsvolle Protokollführung und die administrative Unterstützung von Gremien Freude bereitet.
Sie sich für politischen Prozesse und verwaltungsrechtlichen Fragestellungen interessieren.
es Ihnen leichtfällt, mündlich und schriftlich stilsicher und adressatengerecht zu kommunizieren.

Die Geschäftsprüfungskommission und die Finanzkontrolle
Die Geschäftsprüfungskommission prüft die Amtsführung des Stadtrats und der Verwaltung, den städtischen Haushalt und alle Geschäfte, für welche nicht andere Kommissionen zuständig sind. Der Geschäftsprüfungskommission steht zur Erfüllung ihrer Aufgaben die Finanzkontrolle zur Verfügung.

Die Finanzkontrolle der Stadt erfüllt ihren Auftrag als unabhängiges, politisch neutrales Fachorgan der Finanzaufsicht. Die Finanzkontrolle unterstützt den Stadtrat, die Direktionen, die Verwaltung und die Geschäftsprüfungskommission des Stadtparlaments in Fragen der Aufsicht, der Rechnungslegung und der internen Kontrolle.
Das bieten wir
Es handelt sich um eine vielseitige und verantwortungsvolle Tätigkeit am politischen Puls der Stadt . Im Jahr fallen in der Regel zwölf reguläre Sitzungen an, an denen Ihre Anwesenheit erforderlich ist. Ausserhalb der Sitzungen besteht eine flexible Arbeitszeitgestaltung (Homeoffice möglich).

Es erwarten Sie zeitgemässe Anstellungsbedingungen nach dem Personalrecht der Stadt . Im Rahmen Ihrer Tätigkeit stehen Sie in Kontakt mit der Geschäftsprüfungskommission des Stadtparlaments, dem Stadtrat sowie den Führungsverantwortlichen der Direktionen, Dienststellen und Betrieben der Stadt.

**Darauf kannst Du dich freuen**
* Familiäre Arbeitsatmosphäre: Wir legen Wert auf ein freundliches, unterstützendes Miteinander und kurze Entscheidungswege.
* Attraktive Benefits: Min. 25 Tage Ferien pro Jahr, 13. Monatslohn, Bonusmöglichkeit, Rabatt im Nestlé Shop (vor Ort in Wangen) und vieles mehr.
* Überdurchschnittliche Sozialleistungen: Wir unterstützen dich in verschiedenen Lebensphasen und sorgen für eine ausgewogene Work-Life-Balance.
* Entwicklung: Viele Möglichkeiten zur Karriereentwicklung und persönlichen Entfaltung.
** **
**Ein Blick hinter unsere Kulissen**
Unsere Fabrik ist ein leistungsstarker Produktionsbetrieb der Nestlé Suisse S.A. mit rund 100 Mitarbeitenden und steht für hochwertige Frischteigprodukte, die sowohl in der Schweiz als auch international geschätzt werden.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Produktionsteams suchen wir eine kommunikative und teamorientierte Persönlichkeit als **Operational Excellence Coordinator**. Du treibst Verbesserungen aktiv voran - mit Fokus auf Sicherheit, Qualität und Effizienz sowie eine starke Zusammenarbeit im Betrieb.
** **
**Das erwartet dich bei uns**
* Digitalisierung: Du entwickelst und optimierst digitale Tools und Prozesse für Schichtübergaben, Kennzahlen und Reporting - z.B. mit Power BI oder SharePoint.
* Standardisierung: Du begleitest Teams beim Aufbau, der Umsetzung und Anwendung von Arbeitsanweisungen und Standards in POKA.
* Optimierungsprojekte: Du treibst die Optimierung und Standardisierung von Abläufen und Formatwechseln voran und unterstützt Projekte im Bereich Anlagenoptimierung und Vertical Start-up.
* Analysekompetenz und Kulturförderung: Du unterstützt bei der Analyse von Verlusten, Stillständen und leitest daraus nachhaltige Massnahmen ab, um unsere Prozesse stetig zu optimieren.
* Kompetenzmanagement: Du wirkst beim Aufbau und der Pflege des Kompetenzmanagements und förderst die Weiterentwicklung unserer Mitarbeitenden.
* Kennzahlenmanagement: Du überwachst unsere Produktionskennzahlen und leitest gezielt Verbesserungs-massnahmen ein.
* Kommunikation: Du förderst den Informationsfluss und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Produktion, Technik, Qualität und Verwaltung.
** **
** **
**Das macht Dich erfolgreich**
* Leidenschaft für Produktion: Du hast eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung im Lebensmittelbereich, Erfahrung in der Digitalisierung von Prozessen und optimalerweise eine weiterführende Qualifikation (Studium, HF etc.).
* Organisationsfähigkeit: Fähigkeit, Prioritäten zu setzen und bereichsübergreifend zu denken.
* Methodenwissen: Du hast Erfahrung mit Lean-, TPM- und/oder Continuous-Improvement-Methoden und möchtest deine Kenntnisse anwenden.
* Kommunikationsstärke: Du überzeugst mit zielgerichteter Kommunikation und setzt dich mit Durchsetzungsvermögen und Empathie für gemeinsame Ziele ein
* Team- und Persönlichkeitskompetenz: Du bist zuverlässig, teamorientiert, belastbar, flexibel und serviceorientiert.
* Fit für den Alltag: Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (mind. B2), gute Englischkentnisse sowie gute IT-Kenntnisse (MS Office, SAP und Tools wie Power BI, Sharepoint oder Power Apps) runden dein Profil ab.
**Werde Teil unseres Teams!**
Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der Lebensmittelproduktion und werde Teil der Nestlé-Familie. Be a force for good. Wir freuen uns auf deine vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (Motivationsschreiben, Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse, Diplome etc.) - direkt online!

As an Executive Assistant at Amazon, you will serve as a trusted partner to senior leaders, enabling them to focus on strategic priorities while you manage the complex logistics and operations that keep their organizations running smoothly.

This role offers the opportunity to influence organizational outcomes at country level, collaborate with stakeholders across multiple teams, and drive meaningful improvements to processes that impact how we work. If you are adaptable, detail-oriented, and energized by working in a fast-paced environment, we want to hear from you.

· Manage complex calendars and scheduling for senior leaders, applying an understanding of shifting priorities to ensure the best use of their time across competing demands.

· Prepare, collect, and curate content on behalf of leaders in partnership with key stakeholders, drafting and editing written communications that reflect appropriate tone and nuance.
· Optimize cross-team procedures and processes, identifying opportunities to simplify workflows and implement best practices that benefit the broader organization.
· Coordinate domestic and international travel arrangements, manage expense reporting, and handle purchase orders while ensuring compliance with applicable guidelines.
A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing your leader's calendar, adjusting meetings based on overnight priority shifts and preparing briefing materials for the day ahead. Throughout the day, you move between coordinating a large team event, resolving a scheduling conflict with external partners, mentoring a newer team member on best practices, and pulling together content for an upcoming leadership review. You balance tactical execution with strategic thinking, always staying one step ahead.

Our team is built on a culture of collaboration, trust, and mutual support. We partner closely with leaders and cross-functional teams to ensure organizational priorities move forward efficiently. We are committed to continuous improvement, always looking for ways to raise the bar on how we operate. If you are excited about working in an environment where your contributions directly impact leadership effectiveness and team success, this is the place for you.

* **Contributing to the research and analysis** of scientific literature, government policies, market developments, and company practices to inform campaign planning and identify relevant opportunities.
* **Supporting the creation of campaign outputs** together with internal teams.
* **Contributing to organisation-wide discussions** and fostering knowledge sharing across teams to maximise collective impact for animals.
* **Engaging with external stakeholders** across the *Suisse romande* and representing FOUR PAWS Switzerland in relevant meetings, working groups, media interactions, and presentations.
**Your profile ideally illustrates:**
* Passion for animal welfare and FOUR PAWS vision and mission.
* A degree or initial professional experience in a relevant field such as animal welfare, biology, campaigning, veterinary medicine, communications, marketing, political science, law, or a related discipline.
* Knowledge of the current animal welfare situation in Switzerland.
* Strong organizational and analytical skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* **Fluent French** (spoken and written), **very good English skills**, and the ability to communicate confidently in **German**.
* Motivated, adaptable and driven to make an impact.
* Excellent interpersonal communication and collaboration skills.
* Skilled at turning complex issues into engaging and accessible narratives.
* Willingness to occasionally work at weekend events.

* A multinational team with the spirit of being ONE FOUR PAWS.
* A modern workplace in Zurich, easily accessible by public transport.
* A dog-friendly workplace.
* Time to recharge your batteries: **5 weeks holiday per year** and extra family days at the end of the year.

* Ad\-hoc tasks and projects as required.
Experience Management

* Administer complimentary tickets, invitations and guest lists for clients and partners.
* Coordinate hospitality logistics with promoters and venues.
* Organise internal occasions (e.g. employee events and recognition).
Administrative Support \& Coordination
* Manage the Managing Director's calendar and inbox, prioritise and schedule with foresight.
* Prepare meetings, briefings and presentations (Management Team meetings, Town Halls), take minutes and manage follow\-ups.

* High discretion and reliability in handling confidential information.
* Advanced Outlook and MS Office skills.
* Fluent and English; French is a plus.
* Affinity for live entertainment and hosting, willingness to attend selected evening/weekend events.
